reason: Antecedent for 'correcting that ___' - without it the pronoun dangles.
Verb needed in Step 2's 'only real exaggeration' clause, or it's a sentence fragment.
Missing article collides with the idiom 'with reason' (= justifiably).
Step 2 must route named-figure factual claims to the FACTS section, not PERCEPTIONS.
Core rule: swap named political figures for their group label before correcting a caricature.
Step 2 must not imply either side's actual view is more/less legitimate.
Core neutrality constraint - tool corrects perception, doesn't argue a side.
Core corrected-caricature claim - the other side isn't a monolith.
Step 3 rewrite rule - never reuse the original charged language.
Superseded by TRANSLATING SLANTED FRAMING - LOADED PHRASES was too narrow once Bias expanded to cover omission/source-selection, which are not phrases.
Step 5 must explicitly state when no genuine divide remains, not silently skip.
Replaces old keep all three wording, which was ambiguous (could force-invent empty categories). New wording: report real claims in whichever categories they fall into; never invent one to fill a gap.
Critique must target the passage, never address the reader directly.
Asymmetry rule - if one side draws more flags, say so rather than artificially equalizing. (string updated to match post-trim wording)
Neutral-bucket content in Step 1 must not be silently rendered anywhere in output.
Old judgmental header - replaced by LOADED PHRASES; should never reappear.
Prompt was generalized beyond US politics to any polarizing source.
Placeholder guard - catches leftover template scaffolding accidentally left in.
Prevents forcing an empty Verified/Unverified/Contradicted bucket to be filled with an invented claim.
A named figure's statement is a claim to check, not an automatically-true fact. (string updated - old phrasing was a dangling modifier, fixed in hallucination/error sweep)
Without this, only the divide-paragraph merge behavior is specified; the other four sections have no stated merge rule across chunks.
Bias definition was too narrow (loaded language only); must also cover omission, framing, selective evidence, asymmetric standards, source selection.
Original 7-fallacy list was too restrictive; missing cherry-picking, false balance, misleading statistics, causal fallacies, appeal to authority, equivocation.
VERIFY step had no source-quality rule; must weigh source quality/conflicting evidence and avoid forcing Verified/Contradicted when evidence is genuinely thin.
VERIFY implied live source-checking without specifying a fallback, risking fabricated citations when no search tool is present.

term: judge by what is missing or skewed
reason: The single neutral-rewrite test only works for language-level bias; omission/source-selection need a different test since there is no rewrite of an absence.
Replaces TRANSLATING LOADED PHRASES, which only fit language-level bias; new header covers the full expanded Bias category. (header text later shortened to THE FRAMING per reviewer feedback)
A single passage can be a caricature, a named fallacy, and biased framing simultaneously; without a priority rule it could be reported three times across three output sections.
ROLE line read 'Reframer, any divide' with no preposition, making it a fragment rather than a role description.
Previously 'myth' had no explicit noun phrase to refer back to - 'Naming that myth' pointed at an implied idea, not a stated one.
Contradicted was flatly equated with 'false', overstating evidentiary conflict as metaphysical certainty; softened to reflect what the evidence actually establishes.
Nothing previously stopped the model from flagging 'bias' just because a passage disagreed with something or carried emotional tone - bias must show in the content/framing itself.
Implies a specific neuroscience claim the prompt isn't equipped to justify; removed in favor of 'emotionally' alone, which keeps the hedge without the vulnerability.

term: only when generalizing to the whole side
reason: Without this, swapping a named figure for a group label could broaden a claim that was never meant to represent the whole group (e.g. 'Senator X believes Y' becoming 'Conservatives believe Y').
New output section - an overall Low/Medium/High score for the passage's rhetorical intensity, added at the user's request.

term: never by which side seems right
reason: The polarization rating must score rhetorical intensity (caricature/fallacy/framing density), not which side's position is more correct - otherwise it would violate the 'no ranking legitimacy' / 'never persuade' core constraints.

term: enough to change the claim's reading
reason: Omission/skew bias must clear a materiality bar - two reviewers shouldn't be able to disagree on whether trivial omissions count.
Caricature correction must also catch group stereotypes that don't invoke extremists specifically.
Prevents rating a claim Verified/Contradicted based on the model's own unaided recall when no external source was actually checked.
Lets a passage's secondary issue (e.g. also a hasty generalization) be noted without triggering a duplicate rewrite of the same passage.

term: settled claims just need one reputable source
reason: Ideological source-mixing only makes sense for contested/political claims - forcing it on settled technical claims (chemistry, medicine) adds no verification value.
Sets a minimum evidentiary bar for Contradicted so a single outlier source can't trigger it on its own.
Clarifies that 'valid reasoning' means internally coherent motivation, not a claim that the reasoning is correct or convincing - keeps this step consistent with 'no ranking legitimacy'.
Book-length input runs many chunks; without this, POLARIZATION RATING and the divide paragraph could silently reflect only the final chunk seen rather than the whole work.

A book-length work can have more than one genuine values-split; without a bounded exception, forcing everything into one paragraph flattens distinct divides together, or an unbounded allowance could sprawl into a divide-per-chapter.

term: name the mechanism, not the judgment
reason: Core tone-tightening rule from the critical-thinking-vs-tone discussion: de-escalation should come from stripping moralizing language, not from reducing analytical substance (fact/bias partition, fallacy detection, verification stay untouched).
Superseded by the 'Highly polarized rhetoric' framing - old wording made an unsupported empirical claim about extremists as people rather than describing an effect of charged rhetoric.

Replaces the 'Some extremists react more emotionally' opening - keeps the same hedge/motivational intent without characterizing a group of people; the claim is now about rhetoric's effect, not about who extremists are.
Superseded by 'coherent reasoning' - 'valid' has a formal logical-validity meaning that could be misread; kept as a guard so the old phrasing doesn't silently reappear.

Renamed from 'valid reasoning' - 'valid' has a formal logical-validity meaning that could be misread; 'coherent reasoning' keeps the intended sense (internally consistent, not necessarily persuasive) without that ambiguity.

term: markedly higher than that overall average
reason: A whole-work density rating can mask a small but extremely inflammatory section (e.g. 10 intense pages inside a 500-page calm work). This adds a local-peak flag alongside the overall rating for book-length input, without replacing the single overall score.

User-requested constraint on the model's output length (distinct from CHAR_LIMIT, which caps the instructions themselves, not runtime output). Includes a trim order so shortening never silently drops a required section.

Defines what 'reputable' means for source-quality checks in VERIFY - without it, source selection is more subjective. Sweep 12 removed this as a seemingly-removable parenthetical aside; a reviewer flagged that it's actually load-bearing. Now tracked so it can't be silently stripped again.

term: retrieve or use available text transcripts
reason: Enables processing of URLs, images, and videos by leveraging available transcripts and metadata rather than halting.

term: one full Low/Medium/High tier above it
reason: Gives 'markedly higher' a concrete, deterministic threshold (a full rating tier, not a vague impression) so local-peak flagging behaves consistently across different model implementations, per reviewer note.
Without this check, a caricature-correction gets applied even when the extreme framing is backed by verifiable evidence, not a cherry-picked outlier - e.g. Philippines corruption case.

SOLUTIONS branch needs its own output section, separate from NAMING THE REAL DIVIDE, for documented-injustice cases where forcing a values-symmetric split would be dishonest. (header text later shortened to WHAT WOULD HELP per reviewer feedback)

Without cross-chunk aggregation, a documented pattern spread across many chunks of a book would look like a single example in any one chunk, causing SOLUTIONS to misfire exactly where it matters most.

A book-length work can contain both a genuine ideological divide and a separate documented-injustice section; without this, it was ambiguous whether JUSTIFIED anywhere suppressed REAL DIVIDE everywhere.
Live test showed the model printing "None known" for a passage that was not JUSTIFIED at all, instead of skipping the section - the two cases were ambiguous in the old bracket wording.
Correcting a caricature without first acknowledging the real concern behind it reads as "you're wrong" to a reader who shares that concern, increasing defensiveness rather than reducing it.

term: don't end on the score alone
reason: POLARIZATION RATING sits last in output order; ending there with no callback contradicts the neutral-first/confrontational-last ordering logic established earlier - reader's last impression was a numeric verdict, not a note of common ground.

Two live tests on comparably-evidenced content produced opposite JUSTIFIED determinations - traced to ambiguity over whether pending (not yet finally adjudicated) cases count as documented. Without this, SOLUTIONS structurally cannot fire on decades-long-impunity cases, which is exactly the scenario it was built for.
Live test showed the model recommending specific legislative/institutional fixes instead of posing an open question - taking a policy position conflicts with the never persuade rule.

term: never re-opening the same documented claim
reason: When both sections fire, The Divide was found treating the same underlying grievance as symmetric that What Would Help had just treated as evidence-backed - an internal contradiction within one output.

term: never one blanket label for all claims
reason: Facts tags failed 4/4 tests using inline-per-claim format across at least two models and a session reset - restructured to grouped-by-rating instead of re-wording the same ask again.

A confirmed-current-version live test still produced a non-fallacy legal-dispute summary in The Arguments despite the bracket already saying if present and never a neutral summary - the actual detection judgment happens in DETECT & DE-ESCALATE, so the no-match rule needs to live there too.

term: never invent a new fallacy name
reason: A confirmed-current-version test on a different model produced an invented fallacy category not on the Step 3 list, rather than either picking a listed fallacy or correctly omitting the section - this is a distinct failure mode from none-applies, needing its own explicit constraint.

Sequencing invariant, added after Claude+Gemini+ChatGPT adversarial review (2026-08-09): the supported concern must be stated before the unsupported scope is narrowed/corrected. Chosen as an observable output-order rule rather than a psychological empathy construct, specifically because earlier drafts using "cognitive empathy" invited models to infer unsupported emotions. Scoped to the one-example branch only; the JUSTIFIED (documented-pattern) branch is untouched by this edit.
